text:
Marta L.: Heads-up — staging canary with AWQ-quantized gpt-xx is showing intermittent hangs and repeated tokens since last rollout. seeing it on ~2% of requests :eyes:
Sam K.: ugh. same seed or random? any pattern in prompt length or batch size?
Marta L.: mostly short prompts (<= 64), batch size 1-4. not tied to prompt. sometimes returns a bunch of repeated ' the' tokens, sometimes just hangs until timeout.
Priya N.: can you paste a minimal repro and the serve logs?
Marta L.: here, trimmed logs and the runner command we used:
```
# start canary replica
./awq-runner --model gpt-xx-awq-g4 --group-size 8 --act-quant=true --seed=42 --kv-cache=on
# failing request (raw)
POST /v1/generate
{"prompt":"Write a short haiku about clouds","max_tokens":50}
# logs:
[2027-05-12T14:02:11Z] INFO incoming req id=abc123
[2027-05-12T14:02:11Z] DEBUG awq group=8 seed=42
[2027-05-12T14:02:11Z] WARN token-gen stalled after 1200ms
[2027-05-12T14:02:13Z] ERROR repeated token detected: " the the the the"
```
Sam K.: interesting that WARN shows "token-gen stalled" — could be kv-cache or grp quant kernel. did we change any math kernels in the build?
Evan T.: I rolled a runtime patch 2 days ago that switches AVX path for fp32 fallback. shouldn't affect AWQ quant kernel but maybe the codepath hit for certain alignment.
Priya N.: can we reproduce locally w/ same seed and run the awq offline eval harness? try disabling kv-cache to see if it's cache-related.
Marta L.: tried local reproduce with seed 42 and kv-cache=off: still see repetition but less frequent. with different seed (7) it looks clean.
Sam K.: that points to seed sensitivity. AWQ's group quant uses random dithering for act-quant per-group, plus stochastic rounding in training-mode sim. maybe inference uses a seeded RNG that influences quantization offsets. If two replicas run different RNG states, outputs diverge.
Priya N.: propose steps:
1) run 1000 short prompts across seeds [1..50] on staging canary replica with deterministic RNG pinned and collect repeat rate
2) compare group-size 4/8/16 and act-quant true/false
3) collect perf traces + kernel name from runtime (emit AWQ_KERNEL env)
Sam K.: I'll spin a job. quick script:
```bash
for s in {1..50}; do 
  ./awq-eval --model gpt-xx-awq-g4 --group-size 8 --seed $s --kv-cache=off --tests 200 >> /tmp/awq_seed_results.jsonl
done
```
Evan T.: also add env AWQ_DEBUG_KERNEL=1 to log kernel selection. we had a bug where group-size modulus interacts with vector width and falls back to a scalar path that had a bug.
Marta L.: ok running now (kickoff 1815121200). initial tiny run: seeds 1-10, group=8 -> seeds 2,6 show repeated tokens ~1.5% of requests.
Priya N.: did you try group 16?
Marta L.: group 16 reduced repeats to ~0.2% but latency jumps +12ms p50.
Sam K.: tradeoff: larger group reduces quantization noise but increases compute (and batching pressure). For serving SLOs we can't push group=16 widely. Maybe disable act-quant in production for now?
Evan T.: if act-quant is the issue we can try a hybrid: act-quant=true for long prompts, false for short ones. Or implement a tiny post-filter: detect repeated token sequences and re-roll from a different RNG seed or fallback to int8 variant.
Priya N.: re-roll at inference sounds hacky but feasible as a short-term mitigation. prefer root cause: find scalar kernel bug and patch. I'll look into the kernel code path where group_size % vector_len != 0.
Marta L.: temporary mitigation: revert canary to group=16 + act-quant=true and lower replica weight, then run targeted rollback plan if metrics worsen.
Sam K.: agree. also add turnover test in CI that runs 500 short prompts over 5 seeds to catch seed-dependent regressions.
Evan T.: FYI I've found a suspect in the scalar fallback where a local buffer wasn't zeroed, will push a fix to a feature branch and attach diff.
Marta L.: thanks. once diff lands, i'll re-run seeds 1-50 and report.
ci-bot: Deploy started for branch evan/awq-fix (canary) — status: pending
Priya N.: great. keep notes here. if we still see >0.5% repeats after fix, we'll schedule a rollback.
Marta L.: noted. will update with postfix results (expected ~2h). :thumbsup:
